findings.description: Critical: The shared advisory lock serializes a different-sequence submit/reconcile race but does not make its outcome order-independent. If reconciliation for sequence N commits first, a delayed keyed submit for stale sequence N-1 can acquire the lock afterward and insert a new active row, violating the requirement that the reconciled current sequence be the only active projection row.
findings.resolution: Add a durable per-change reconciliation high-water/current-generation record (or equivalent database invariant) that reconciliation advances in the same transaction and keyed submit consults while holding the same lock, so a submit older than the authoritative generation is rejected or created terminal/cancelled. Specify and test both forced transaction orders, including reconcile-commits-before-stale-submit.

findings.description: Nit: The new reconcile endpoint requires policy denial behavior, but the plan never identifies the authorization action. The current native and Cedar inventories know `submit_work`, not `reconcile_work`, while the coordinator package cannot modify the policy schema or policy files under its declared write scope.
findings.resolution: Specify that `/work/reconcile` authorizes through the existing `submit_work` action (with reconciliation context), or explicitly add the policy/Cedar files and tests to package scope if a new action is intended.

findings.description: Nit: The verification gates promise direct MCP parity but run no dedicated direct-MCP test module and no whole coordinator test directory. A new direct MCP test file can therefore be omitted from both package and integration gates while all declared commands remain green.
findings.resolution: Name the direct MCP projection test module in both verification commands, or run a suitably bounded test directory/marker that necessarily includes the direct and proxy transport parity tests from task 1.7.

findings.description: The plan correctly places same-key idempotency in PostgreSQL with a partial unique expression index and keeps unkeyed submissions backward compatible.
findings.resolution: Preserve the database-owned uniqueness invariant and exact conflict-target integration test during implementation.

findings.description: The persist-before-project seam and resume re-derivation keep filesystem state authoritative and give the non-transactional crash window an explicit repair path.
findings.resolution: Preserve the ordering and queue-response non-authority tests during implementation.
